panels.description: Chart 9-style: S&P 500 in real stuff, not dollars. Live series is Invesco DB Commodity (DBC), a daily fund that tracks a broad commodity basket: energy (crude, heating oil, natural gas), industrial and precious metals, and agriculture — the stuff you buy, or that goes into the stuff you buy. Same daily divide as S&P / gold. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.
panels.title: S&P 500 / commodities

panels.description: Chart 10-style: S&P 500 in food and fiber. Live series is Invesco DB Agriculture (DBA): corn, wheat, soybeans, sugar, coffee, cocoa, live cattle, and similar — the stuff you eat and wear, not oil or copper. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.
panels.title: S&P 500 / agricultural index

panels.description: Chart 12-style: S&P 500 in industrial metals. Live series is Invesco DB Base Metals (DBB): aluminum, copper, and zinc — the steel / copper / zinc basket the book uses for automakers’ costs. Not gold or silver. Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.
panels.title: S&P 500 / industrial metals

panels.description: Chart 13-style: relative performance from the left edge of the dashboard range (all three start at 0%). The book starts at the 2001 precious-metals bull; set a custom range such as 2001-01-01 to 2008-04-01 to match that figure. S&P 500 (FMP ^GSPC), gold (GCUSD), and silver (SIUSD). Use a multi-year range; Last 1 hour has no daily bars.
panels.title: Relative performance of S&P 500, gold, and silver

panels.description: Chart 16-style cumulative price rise from the left edge of the dashboard range (both lines start at 0%). Official is the IMF/BLS CPI-U index divided by its first print in this range. The 1980-method line compounds that official monthly change plus an extra 7 percentage points per year (Williams’ published ShadowStats add-back for OER, substitution, and hedonics). Set 1980 to now to see the long compounding gap. Not a licensed ShadowStats file.

custom.axisLabel: cumulative rise from start of range
